questions.question: The three pressures making energy management unavoidable for South Africa are:
options: Supply strain proven by load-shedding, climate-and-trade pressure including carbon border taxes, and equity — wasted energy is development lost
Falling coal prices, rising exports and tourism
Population decline, urban shrinkage and deflation
Cheap electricity, abundant water and low demand

questions.question: A greener economy is defined as:
options: An economy based only on agriculture
One that grows while its resource use and emissions shrink — decoupling prosperity from pollution
One that exports only renewable electricity

questions.question: Efficiency is called the invisible power station because:
options: Renewable plants are hard to see
Saving one station's worth of demand is cheaper, faster and cleaner than building one, and emits nothing

questions.question: Carbon border taxes threaten South African exports because:
options: Ships must now burn cleaner fuel
Products made with coal-heavy electricity pay penalties at rich-country borders — the dirty grid becomes a tax on every exported ton

questions.question: The Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) is:
options: The official electricity roadmap setting what retires and what gets built by which year — the document investors, Eskom and municipalities steer by

questions.question: South Africa's carbon tax works by:
options: Making emitters pay per ton of carbon dioxide, nudging industry toward cleaner processes — the first tax of its kind in Africa

questions.question: The 'quiet rules' that save more energy than most headline projects are:
options: Building energy-performance regulations, appliance labelling, and minimum efficiency standards banning the worst products

questions.question: The Just Energy Transition Partnership channels international finance into:
options: Grid building, coal-town retraining and green industry — pledged in the tens of billions of dollars

questions.question: An energy audit is:
options: A metered walk through a firm's operations finding where energy is wasted — leaks, worn motors, uninsulated pipes — with fixes ranked by payback
A tax inspection of electricity bills
A count of the firm's generators

questions.question: Wheeling allows a company to:
options: Transport coal by road instead of rail
Generate power at a sunny site and consume it, via the grid, at another site

questions.question: A product's carbon footprint has become a matter of market access because:
options: Footprints are printed on packaging by law worldwide
European carbon border rules tax the emissions embedded in imports, and banks and investors screen for climate risk

questions.question: Greenwashing is:
options: Marketing an unchanged, polluting operation as eco-friendly — the opposite of measured baseline-target-audit-report management

questions.question: The single hungriest machine in a typical home is:
options: The electric geyser, often around 40 per cent of the bill

questions.question: The geyser efficiency ladder runs:
options: Thermostat to 60 degrees, insulating blanket, timer, and ultimately a solar water heater or heat pump so the sun does the heaviest job
Turn the thermostat to maximum for faster heating
Run the geyser only at the evening peak

questions.question: LEDs are 'the cheap victory' because:
options: They give the same light for about a tenth of the electricity of incandescent bulbs and last years longer
They cool the room while lighting it

questions.question: The 'citizen layer' of individual energy management includes:
options: Shifting use off-peak, turning homes into micro power stations with rooftop PV, and supporting the plans and lines the transition needs

questions.question: Redrawing the energy problem as a leaking bucket shifts attention to:
options: Plugging the holes — waste in buildings, bulbs, geysers and motors — rather than only pouring in more supply

questions.question: The comparison between a new station and plugging holes shows:
options: Both cost the same over ten years
A station costs hundreds of billions and takes a decade, while efficiency costs a fraction, works within months and emits nothing
Stations are faster to build than to insulate

questions.question: The one-line summary of the entire topic is:
options: The kilowatt-hour you never use is the cheapest and cleanest one there is

questions.question: The government spanner is 'the big one' because:
options: Only government can write the rules — the IRP roadmap, auctions, carbon tax, building rules, labels and the just transition money

questions.question: The business spanner 'turns the biggest bolts' because:
options: Firms use most of the country's energy, so audits, rooftop solar and clean supply chains move the largest numbers
Only businesses pay the carbon tax

questions.question: 'Foreign buyers now ask how much smoke is inside your product' refers to:
options: Carbon footprint reporting and border carbon rules turning a dirty grid into a trade problem — cleaning up as strategy, not charity

questions.question: The warning label on the business spanner reads:
options: No greenwashing — painting the logo green while changing nothing fools nobody for long

questions.question: The stadium wave answers the question of individual impact by showing:
options: The evening peak is millions of private choices landing together — one arm cannot make a wave, but the wave is nothing except arms
Sport is the biggest energy user

questions.question: The plays ranked by size start with:
options: The geyser — the hungriest machine — then lighting, kitchen habits, winter sealing, standby and transport

questions.question: 'Heat the person, not the ceiling' recommends:
options: Sealing gaps, insulating, and wearing warm clothing before heating whole rooms

questions.question: The closing summary of the whole topic assigns the roles:
options: Individuals write rules, government turns bolts
Business writes the roadmap, households audit factories
Government acts alone while others watch
Government writes the rules, business turns the big bolts, and sixty million households are the wave — with the unused kilowatt-hour as champion
